test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The selling price of 34 books is equal to the cost price of 17 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **Selling Price** of x articles is equal to the **Cost Price** of y articles, then:

Ratio of **CP : SP** = x : y = 34 : 17 = 2 : 1.

Loss = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

**Loss %** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 2) × 100 = 50%.

Since CP > SP, it is a **loss**.

**∴ The correct answer is 50% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP of 34 books = CP of 17 books.

**Formulas:** Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/425c8d6ad96e04366696a20d3ad9bd5a9d4545244ca9ce5ceaf3c4a0244e0aab.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 book be 1 unit.

⇒ Total **CP of 34 books** = 34 units.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** of 34 books = CP of 17 books = 17 units.

⇒ **Loss** = CP − SP = 34 − 17 = 17 units.

⇒ **Loss %** = (17 ÷ 34) × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Articles

When the cost price of 'm' articles is equal to the selling price of 'n' articles, Gain/Loss% = (m − n) ÷ n × 100. A positive result indicates gain, and a negative result indicates loss.

Profit Condition

Profit occurs only when the **Selling Price** is greater than the **Cost Price** (SP > CP).</p
